key_insight: PD-CogT-Sleep will test whether auditory stimulation targeting deep sleep enhances cognitive training benefits in people with Parkinson’s disease and mild cognitive impairment.
clinical_relevance: If effective, this remotely delivered, non-pharmacological approach could help improve cognitive training responsiveness, but benefits are not yet established.
method: Single-center, partly decentralized, double-blind randomized sham-controlled trial targeting 50 participants.
Participants randomized 1:1 to digital cognitive training plus phase-targeted auditory stimulation or sham stimulation.
Executive function is the primary outcome; additional measures include cognition, participant reports, blood biomarkers, and sleep EEG.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a trial protocol with assessments at baseline, five weeks post-allocation, and three-month follow-up; no outcome results are reported.
watch_item: The planned small, single-center study may limit generalizability and cannot by itself establish long-term disease modification.
paper_title: Enhancing deep sleep with auditory stimulation to boost cognitive training responsiveness in people with Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment: Rationale and design of the double-blind randomized controlled trial PD-CogT-Sleep
